Subject: Pricing breakdown request: US vs EU routing + residency adder

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking the time last week. As we scope our pilot for Acme Financial's European subsidiary, we need a clear, line-itemable price breakdown for your hosted API across regions and any data residency "adders" that would apply when routing to EU-only infrastructure.

High-level asks:
- Baseline per-1k-token rate for US-hosted traffic vs EU-hosted traffic (we need to show this to Finance)
- Data-residency surcharge (if any): how is it charged (per-token / per-request / monthly flat fee)?
- Invoice tagging or billing by legal entity: can Redwood issue separate invoices per Acme EU Sarl vs Acme US Inc?
- Impact on discounts / committed spend: do residency addons reduce volume for discount tiers?

We also need a sample invoice (one line per region, clear line items) we can use for procurement. Can you attach the current rate card and a sample invoice?

Target timeline: procurement wants final numbers by EOD Thursday (Dec 24) to include in the Q4 budget.

Thanks,
Emily

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acmefin.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-20T13:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pricing breakdown request: US vs EU routing + residency adder

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our December rate card and a sample invoice that shows per-legal-entity tagging. Quick summary below; details are in the PDF/Excel.

Short summary (baseline hosted API):
- US (multi-tenant, us-central): $0.80 per 1k prompt tokens / $0.85 per 1k completion tokens
- EU (multi-tenant, eu-west): +18% regional premium compared to US (example: $0.94 per 1k prompt tokens / $1.00 per 1k completion tokens)
- Data residency adder: optional +$0.25 per 1k tokens when requests are pinned to a residency-only host (dedicated isolated routing to EU-only infra). This adder is applied per-token (prompt + completion) and appears as a separate line on invoices.

Discounts / committed spend:
- Committed monthly spend reduces the net unit price; residency adder is additive after discounts. Example: 12-month commit of $150k/mo -> 15% off base token rates, then residency adder applied to the discounted subtotal.
- Residency adder does not count toward the committed spend threshold (we do not count adders for tier qualification) — happy to discuss alternate treatment if Acme requires it for accounting.

Invoicing and tagging:
- We can issue separate invoices per legal entity if you provide billing contacts and tax details for Acme EU Sarl and Acme US Inc.
- Sample invoice (attached) shows: region_code, model, tokens, residency_flag, unit_price, line_total. We can also push a CSV export to your SFTP nightly.

Operational notes:
- Routing: you can choose "region-prefer" (best-effort routing with fallbacks) or "region-strict" (requests only served from EU nodes; triggers residency adder). Region-strict will have the residency adder and slightly higher p50 latency.
- If you need per-request residency guarantees + audit log evidence (for procurement), we have an add-on with signed logs and KMS integration — that is a separate compliance package.

Attachments:
- Redwood_rate_card_DEC2026.pdf
- residency-sample-invoice.xlsx

If you want, I can build two scenarios: 1) pilot traffic 250M tokens/mo and 2) production 2B tokens/mo, showing effective blended unit prices and invoice samples — should I go ahead?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 650 555 0199

(Attachments: Redwood_rate_card_DEC2026.pdf, residency-sample-invoice.xlsx)

Vanessa — thanks, that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups:

1) The residency adder not counting toward committed-spend tiers will be an issue for our Finance team — they prefer all billable items to count toward the commit. Would Redwood consider counting a portion (e.g., 50%) of the residency adder toward tier qualification?

2) Can you do separate invoices with NET 60 payment terms for the EU legal entity? Our EU treasury asks for NET 60.

3) For procurement approval, we need a one-time pilot discount for the first 3 months (15% off blended spend) to get internal sign-off. Is that something you can offer for the pilot only?

If you can confirm those three items and provide the two-scenario blended pricing, we should be able to move this to procurement next week.

Thanks,
Emily
